collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 3-8; in the story (name1)'s face is shaped differently, with one side smaller than the other)

collection.description: A small child stares at a villager whose face is shaped differently, to the parent's dismay: wave, or let the parent see to it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s face is shaped differently: one side is smaller than the other, and (subject.his/her) mouth sits a little to one side. (subject.He/she) is used to being looked at. Today a small child, (friend), is staring at (subject.him/her) with total concentration across the clearing, and (friend)'s parent is mortified, trying to turn the child's head away.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) carries on with (subject.his/her) work. Later, (friend)'s parent comes over, embarrassed, to apologize. (subject) shakes (subject.his/her) head. "Don't. Just tell (friend.him/her) my name, so next time (friend.he/she) can say hello instead of staring." The next time, (friend) yells "HELLO (subject)!" across the whole village at the top of (friend.his/her) voice. It's an improvement.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) waves. (friend) waves back. (subject) pulls a funny face. (friend) pulls one back. (subject) walks over, says hello to the parent, and says, "Kids look. It's fine. They're working things out." (subject.He/she) crouches down. "Hello. I'm (subject). My face is like this. What's yours like?" (friend) shows (friend.his/her) face, scrunched up as far as it will go. They both laugh.
